label: First copy step echoing an initial "n" (L>=6)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at the step right after <DEL> where the fed-back input is the first original token (recall_idx 1, prev_tok <DEL>), and only when that token is "n" (99.9% of mass). Needs longer sequences: it is silent for L=3-4, close to zero for L=5, and active for L>=6. Magnitude grows with L: activation mass share goes 0.11/0.22/0.31/0.36 for L=6..9 on similar step counts. Does not fire on n during the original phase, on later copy steps, or on any other first token (the rare weak hits on f/g/y first tokens are about 0.01-0.1 of max). False positives are a few L=6 cases where n appears again inside the sequence.

issues: Small inaccuracy: the explanation says the false positives are L=6 sequences where 'n' appears again. Some test false positives have no repeated n, e.g. 'n t v i e g' and 'n 3 w x i x'. There are only 19 of them against about 11k predicted steps, so this is noise, not a systematic class.
L=5 is not exactly zero. On test, 8% of L=5 steps with a first 'n' fire (precision 0.079 on 2749 steps), but they hold only 0.14% of activation mass. This is consistent with 'close to zero for L=5'.

The missed activations (473 test steps, 0.2% of mass) are weak (0.00-0.05 of max). They are mostly recall_idx 1 at L=9 with a non-n first token, often with 'n' as the second token, plus a few L=5 sequences starting with 'n'. All are low-mass, and the non-n L=9 class scores precision 0.003, so no predicate would capture them usefully.
The ablations confirm the L>=6 condition. Without it, test F1 is 0.798. With L>=5 instead, test F1 is 0.889. With L>=6, test F1 is 0.978 and mass recall 0.998.
